components.input_conditions: Finite feasible data satisfying thm.P008.interpolation with 0≤μ<L<∞.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: No dimension enlargement; transformed curvature 1/(L−μ). No evaluation-cost bound is given.
components.preserved_model_properties: Original dimension d, values f_i and gradients g_i are realized; output belongs to F_{μ,L}.
remaining_obligations: A specific lower-bound application must supply hidden information and Algorithm coverage.
Adaptive extension consistency, randomized lifting, output restrictions and information-to-error conversion require separate arguments.
Charge computation of conjugates separately if an executable realization is required.
components.transformation: Subtract μ curvature from the data, conjugate the transformed triples, construct H as a finite maximum of quadratics, then conjugate back and restore μ curvature.

construction.definition: For s=L−μ>0 set a_i=g_i−μx_i and b_i=<x_i,g_i>−f_i−μ||x_i||²/2. Define H(z)=max_{i∈I}{b_i+<x_i,z−a_i>+||z−a_i||²/(2s)}. With H*(x)=sup_z{<x,z>−H(z)}, output the mathematical function f(x)=H*(x)+μ||x||²/2. These are Remark 2's transformed triples and maximum-of-quadratics construction, with H renamed to distinguish it from the original f. For feasible data this realizes f(x_i)=f_i and ∇f(x_i)=g_i in F_{μ,L}.
construction.hidden_objects: No hidden distribution, direction or index is introduced by this construction. A lower-bound application must separately specify what is hidden from its Algorithm.
construction.parameters: d≥1; finite nonempty I; x_i,g_i∈R^d, f_i∈R; 0≤μ<L<∞. All ordered pairs must satisfy thm.P008.interpolation's condition.
construction.public_information: The construction takes the full finite data and μ,L as inputs. Remark 2 supplies a mathematical interpolant, not an adversarial disclosure protocol.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Curator scope restriction, not a source theorem asserting an escape strategy or a proved lower bound.
escape_conditions.statement: Queries at unregistered points and unrestricted outputs are not controlled by this interpolation certificate. No lower-bound conclusion for such Algorithms is part of this record.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Once data are fixed, f is fixed. No history-dependent choice rule or consistency theorem for extending adaptively selected data is supplied here.
oracle_realizations.cost: Remark 2 supplies no query-complexity or arithmetic-cost bound for evaluating the conjugate. No computational implementation cost is identified with one Oracle call.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: None established. Finite interpolation feasibility alone does not constrain information in answers outside the registered sites.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: No error lower bound is supplied. Any conversion from a transcript limitation to an output gap must be proved separately.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: For the constructed fixed f, a first-order query at x∈R^d can be specified mathematically as returning (f(x),∇f(x)); at registered sites the return is exactly (f_i,g_i). This describes the function's oracle, not an efficient implementation of conjugate evaluation.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: Deterministic fixed function; repeated queries have identical exact answers. No stochastic oracle or sample coupling is specified.

content.proof_support: The complete local construction argument is explicitly separated from source text in thm.P008.interpolation, #/content/proofs/1/full_local_argument; its independent checking remains required before acceptance.
